title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Working Regulations for Specially Invited Consultants of the Supreme People's Court
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Working Rules for Specially Invited Consultants of the Supreme People's Court

Fa Fa [2009] No. 32

Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

As required by work, the Working Rules for Specially Invited Consultants of the Supreme People's Court have been revised and adopted by the Leading Party Members' Group of the Supreme People's Court. They are hereby issued to you for your support and cooperation in your work.

May 31, 2009

Working Rules for Specially Invited Consultants of the Supreme People's Court

(Revised on May 26, 2009)

Article 1  These Rules are formulated in accordance with work requirements in order to fully leverage the role of specially invited consultants, further broaden the channels and means for understanding public opinion, improve and refine the scientific and democratic decision-making mechanism, and continuously promote the scientific development of the work of the People's Courts.

Article 2  Specially invited consultants of the Supreme People's Court are individuals appointed by the Supreme People's Court to provide consultation and suggestions on the trial work, team building, and judicial reform of the People's Courts.

Article 3  Specially invited consultants of the Supreme People's Court shall be renowned experts, scholars, and prominent figures in the fields of humanities and social sciences, such as politics, law, philosophy, history, economics, and sociology.

Article 4  Specially invited consultants are appointed by the Supreme People's Court, each term lasting five years.

Upon expiration of the term, they may be reappointed for one additional term. Consecutive appointments shall not exceed two terms.

Article 5  Duties of specially invited consultants:

(1) To provide advisory opinions on the implementation of the Party's line, principles, and policies by the People's Courts, as well as on the implementation of major work deployments of the Party Central Committee and the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress;

(2) To provide advisory opinions and suggestions on the formulation of major work decisions and important judicial policies by the People's Courts, on advancing the reform of the judicial system and working mechanisms, on strengthening team building, and on drafting judicial interpretations and important work reports;

(3) To make suggestions on the fair adjudication of cases and enforcement work by the People's Courts in accordance with the law;

(4) To reflect or transmit the opinions of the public regarding instances where the People's Courts or judicial personnel fail to handle cases according to law during judicial activities, thereby affecting judicial fairness.

Article 6  Specially invited consultants enjoy the following rights in performing their duties:

(1) To participate in meetings of specially invited consultants and research activities in their personal capacity, and to independently express advisory opinions;

(2) To access, through the Supreme People's Court, relevant materials necessary for performing their duties;

(3) To put forward opinions and suggestions regarding the conduct and organization of specific advisory work.

Article 7  Specially invited consultants shall assume the following obligations in performing their duties:

(1) Not to engage in work or activities inconsistent with the nature of the specially invited consultant's role, using the identity of a specially invited consultant of the Supreme People's Court;

(2) To protect state secrets and secrets related to trial work.

Article 8  The Supreme People's Court shall convene a working meeting of specially invited consultants once each year.

As required by work, forums may be convened from time to time to seek opinions from some specially invited consultants on specific special tasks.

Specially invited consultants may submit advisory opinions and suggestions at any time regarding specific tasks of the People's Courts.

Article 9  To facilitate specially invited consultants' understanding of the work of the People's Courts, the Supreme People's Court shall provide specially invited consultants with relevant documents and materials of the Supreme People's Court, and subscribe to the People's Court Daily, the Supreme People's Court Gazette, and other materials relevant to the work of specially invited consultants.

Local People's Courts at all levels and special People's Courts shall provide support, cooperation, and convenience for the work of specially invited consultants.

Article 10  With respect to recommendations and suggestions for improvement made by specially invited consultants, the relevant People's Courts shall handle them diligently and provide feedback on the handling situation and results to the specially invited consultant who made the recommendations and suggestions.

Article 11  Where a specially invited consultant falls under any of the following circumstances during their term of office, the Supreme People's Court shall dismiss them:

(1) They submit a written request for resignation;

(2) Due to a change in position, it is no longer appropriate to continue serving as a specially invited consultant;

(3) Other circumstances where it is inappropriate to continue serving as a specially invited consultant.

Article 12  The Supreme People's Court shall establish an Office for Specially Invited Consultants, which shall be located within the People's Supervision Work Office of the Supreme People's Court and shall be responsible for daily administrative affairs.

Article 13  These Rules shall take effect from the date of promulgation.
